sketches: The target posits, for every radius r, a second phase transition threshold t(n) for r-neighbourhood shotgun reconstructibility of G(n,p); the source asks to determine that sharp threshold for the two unresolved radii r ∈ {1,2}, i.e. it is the r <= 2 instance of the general threshold statement.

source.name: Second phase transition in r-neighbourhood shotgun assembly
source.statement: It seems likely that for every radius $r$ there should be a second phase transition around some threshold $t=t(n)$. By which we mean that, if $p=\omega(t(n))$, then $G$ is with high probability reconstructible from its $r$-neighbourhoods, while if $p=o(t(n))$ and $p=\omega(n^{-\frac{2r+1}{2r}})$, then with high probability $G$ is not reconstructible from its $r$-neighbourhoods.
source.context: The paper establishes the existence of this second phase transition for all $r\geq 3$, but the question remains open for $r=1$ and $r=2$, for which only improved (but not matching) bounds are given.

target.name: Sharp threshold for r-reconstructibility in G(n,p)
target.statement: [Full statement text was not included in the supplied input; the environment is labelled \texttt{[qu]\ Question} and, from context, concerns the exact threshold for $r$-reconstructibility of $\mathcal{G}(n,p)$ for $r\in\{1,2\}$, the two radii for which the paper provides only upper and lower bounds rather than a sharp threshold.]
target.context: The paper determines the sharp threshold for $r$-reconstructibility for every $r\geq 3$. For $r=2$ it improves bounds of Gaudio and Mossel by polynomial factors, and for $r=1$ it sharpens a result of Huang and Tikhomirov, but in neither case is the exact threshold pinned down.

sketches: The paper states (context of Conjecture 3.1) that the disproportionate bipartition statement for measures on S^1 would imply, by a simple inductive argument splitting [n]=P∪Q and recursing on each interval, that f(n) ≤ 2n−2; the matching lower bound f(n) ≥ 2n−2 is already proved via Segal-Halevi's construction. Hence Conjecture 3.1 implies f(n)=2n−2.

source.name: Disproportionate bipartition of measures on S¹
source.statement: For any $n \geq 2$ non-atomic probability measures $\mu_1, \mu_2, \ldots, \mu_n$ on the unit circle $S^1$ and non-negative reals $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \ldots, \alpha_n$ summing to $1$, there exists a partition of the set $[n] = P \cup Q$ into two nonempty sets and a partition of the circle $S^1 = X \cup X^c$ into two intervals such that $$\min_{i \in P} \mu_i(X) = \sum_{j \in P} \alpha_j \quad \text{and} \quad \min_{i \in Q} \mu_i(X^c) = \sum_{j \in Q} \alpha_j.$$
source.context: The authors introduce this conjecture as a topological measure-partitioning statement whose truth would imply, by a simple inductive argument, that $f(n) = 2n-2$ for all $n \geq 2$, which would be optimal for disproportionate division. The $n=2$ case is known and is essentially the Stromquist–Woodall theorem, but the conjecture is open already for $n=3$.

target.name: Disproportionate division requires 2n−2 cuts
target.statement: We suspect that the above construction reflects the truth and that $f(n) = 2n - 2$ for all $n \geq 2$.
target.context: The authors give a construction (attributed to Segal-Halevi [6]) showing $f(n) \geq 2n-2$ for all $n \geq 2$, where $f(n)$ is the maximum number of cuts needed for disproportionate division with $n$ agents. Theorem 1.1 establishes $f(n) \leq 3n-4$, leaving a gap. The authors believe the lower bound is tight and that the truth is $f(n) = 2n-2$.

sketches: The paper states explicitly that Conjecture 4 (vec-t(n)=Θ(√(n/log n))) follows from Conjecture 3 (vec-a(n)=Θ(√(n log n))): the inequality vec-t(n) ≥ n/vec-a(n) turns the conjectured upper bound O(√(n log n)) on the acyclic number into the missing lower bound Ω(√(n/log n)) on the dichromatic number, while the upper bound vec-t(n) ≤ (√2+o(1))√(n/log n) is already proved.

source.name: Acyclic number Θ(√(n log n)) oriented triangle-free
source.context: The paper establishes $\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\varepsilon\right)\sqrt{n\log n}\leq\vec{a}(n)\leq\frac{107}{8}\sqrt{n}\log n$, a logarithmic gap between lower and upper bounds. The authors believe the upper bound can be sharpened to $C\sqrt{n\log n}$ by analysing a suitable orientation of the triangle-free process $G_{\triangle}$.

target.name: Maximum dichromatic number of oriented triangle-free graphs
target.context: Conjecture 4 follows from Conjecture 3, since $\vec{t}(n)\geq n/\vec{a}(n)$ and $\vec{t}(n)\leq t(n)$. The paper establishes $\frac{8}{107}\frac{\sqrt{n}}{\log n}\leq\vec{t}(n)\leq\left(\sqrt{2}+o(1)\right)\sqrt{\frac{n}{\log n}}$, leaving a logarithmic gap on the lower side.

sketches: U_t(n) is the minimum number of lazy transpositions in a t-uniformity network on n positions (shuffling t distinguishable counters), and the companion papers are by the same authors. Setting t=2 in the conjectured formula U_t(n)=tn−C(t+1,2) gives exactly 2n−3, which is the statement of Conjecture 1 in 2208.06630. So the 2-uniformity conjecture is the t=2 instance of the general problem.

source.name: Exact formula for U_t(n) lazy transpositions
source.context: This generalises Problem 1 to the setting of shuffling $t$ distinguishable counters across $n$ positions using the fewest lazy transpositions. The upper bound $U_t(n)\leq tn-\binom{t+1}{2}$ is achieved by existing sweeping/divide-and-conquer constructions. When $t=n$ the problem reduces to Problem 1, which Theorem 2 answers negatively; the paper asks whether the trivial bound is tight for other values of $t$.

target.name: Minimum lazy transpositions in 2-uniformity networks
target.statement: For $n\geq 2$, the minimum number of lazy transpositions in a 2-uniformity network is $2n-3$.
target.context: The authors construct a 2-uniformity network of length $2n-3$ using the sequence $(1,2,\tfrac{1}{2}),(1,3,\tfrac{2}{n}),(1,2,\tfrac{1}{2}),(1,4,\tfrac{2}{n-1}),\dots,(1,2,\tfrac{1}{2}),(1,n,\tfrac{2}{3}),(1,2,\tfrac{1}{2})$, and conjecture this is optimal. They remark that, if true, it would match nicely with selection networks.
